subject: Introduction to our small-firm partner
body:
Hi Henry,

Thank you for the frank conversation on Friday. As we discussed, our enterprise tier is far more than a solo practice needs, so I'd like to introduce you to Fogg & Partners, our implementation partner for smaller firms. They can set you up on the starter edition in an afternoon.

I've copied Phileas Fogg here. All the best with the new engagements.

Sophie

subject: Re: Introduction to our small-firm partner
body:
Dear Sophie,

Most kind of you, and a sensible suggestion; I had suspected as much. I shall arrange a time with Mr Fogg this week. Should my practice grow to the point where your enterprise offering makes sense, you will be the first to hear of it.

With thanks,
Henry Watson

subject: Introduction to your IT team?
body:
Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking my call last week, and for being so clear that office facilities rather than business software sit with you. Would you be comfortable introducing me to whoever leads IT or business applications at Nakatomi? A short intro email is plenty; I'll take it from there and keep you out of the follow-up.

Thanks again,
Mike

subject: Re: Introduction to your IT team?
body:
Hi Mike,

Our IT director is Harold Takagi, but he guards his inbox closely and doesn't take vendor intros well. I'll mention your name at our next leadership meeting and let you know if he's interested. I can't promise more than that, sorry! Good luck.

Grace

subject: Stark three-year expansion: agreement out for signature
body:
Hi Priya,

As promised, the three-year expansion agreement is out for signature in DocuSign. It covers the 200 additional seats and the premium service tier, and it keeps your current per-seat rate locked through 2029. I've attached a one-page summary for your finance team with the commitment year by year.

Kevin asked last week about staggering the new seats. That's built in: we'd bring them on in two waves of 100, six weeks apart.

Anything that needs another pass, send it my way.

Jenna

subject: Your Wonka workspace: team plan options
body:
Hi Layla,

I noticed your team has invited nine people to the self-serve workspace in the last two weeks, which is great to see. At that size the team plan usually works out cheaper than individual seats, and it adds shared brand-asset libraries and approval workflows, which I think your launch calendar would use.

No pressure at all. I can set up a 20-minute walkthrough, or simply send the comparison sheet.

Sophie

subject: Re: Your Wonka workspace: team plan options
body:
Hi Sophie,

Thanks for reaching out! The comparison sheet would be helpful. We're happy on self-serve for now, but Charlotte runs our e-commerce side and might want the approval workflows for the holiday range. I'll loop her in if it gets serious. Until then, please don't book anything with the wider team.

Layla

subject: Sterling Cooper: updated order form
body:
Hi Mason,

Attached is the updated order form reflecting what we agreed on Friday: 75 seats, a two-year term, and the creative-review add-on included at no charge for year one. I've also added the termination-for-convenience clause your team asked for, limited to the first 90 days.

Once you're comfortable, Joan's team could start the vendor review in parallel, so we're not waiting on procurement at the very end.

Thanks,
Sophie

subject: The store operations benchmark you asked about
body:
Hi Nathan,

I appreciate the honest 'not now', and I won't keep chasing. Before I step back, here's the store-operations benchmark you mentioned on our first call: how three national chains cut district-manager reporting time by about a third.

No reply needed. I'll check in again in Q3, when your planning cycle opens.

Best,
Jenna

subject: Globex MSA: our legal team's responses to the redlines
body:
Hi David,

Our legal team has turned around Michael's redlines on the MSA. We accepted the liability cap at twelve months of fees and the data processing addendum as written. The one open point is the auto-renewal notice period, where we proposed 60 days instead of 90. Clean and tracked versions are attached.

If Michael is comfortable, the order form for the enterprise implementation can go out the same day. Could we take 20 minutes on Thursday to walk through the onboarding timeline?

Best,
Jenna

subject: Blue Sun multi-region: next step with your CISO
body:
Hi Hudson,

Thanks for the session yesterday. As we discussed, the multi-region deployment is settled technically; the gating item is Ingrid's security sign-off. Could you introduce me, or forward the attached architecture summary covering regional data residency, SSO enforcement and our penetration-test cadence?

I'd like 45 minutes with her and our security lead before the end of April so we hold the end-of-May target.

Mike

subject: HRIS integration: scoping questions
body:
Hi Aisha,

Thanks for walking me through how your people team works today. To scope the HRIS integration properly, could you confirm three things: which HRIS you're on, whether you want new hires provisioned automatically, and who on your side would own the integration once it's live?

This is a slightly unusual project for us, so I'd like to get the scoping right rather than fast.

Jenna

subject: Invitation: customer advisory board
body:
Hi Priya,

Your team gives us some of the sharpest product feedback we receive, so I'd love to invite you to our customer advisory board. It meets virtually once a quarter for 90 minutes, and the first session in May covers our analytics roadmap for the second half of the year.

There's no commitment beyond that. Let me know and I'll send the calendar hold.

Sophie

subject: Re: Blue Sun multi-region: next step with your CISO
body:
Mike,

Sent your summary to Ingrid and copied you on the intro. Fair warning: her team is buried in an internal audit until early May, so she may be slow to respond. She did say regional data residency is her main question, so the summary should help when she gets to it.

Hudson

subject: Re: Globex MSA: our legal team's responses to the redlines
body:
Jenna,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I've passed the redlines to Michael, but procurement has a queue right now, so I can't promise a date. The onboarding timeline looks right to me.

One ask: can you confirm the implementation team would be the same people who ran the POC with us in March? That continuity matters to my engineers. Thursday doesn't work this week; let's aim for next week.

David

subject: Re: Invitation: customer advisory board
body:
Hi Sophie,

I'd be delighted, thank you for thinking of us. Count me in for May. Could you send the hold to my calendar and to Ben Okoro as an optional attendee? He's keen to hear where the roadmap is going before our planning in the autumn.

Priya

subject: Re: HRIS integration: scoping questions
body:
Hi Jenna,

We're on Workday. Yes, automatic provisioning for new hires and deprovisioning for leavers is the main goal. Caroline Ward runs the HRIS and would own it; I'll introduce you once we're through our planning cycle. Realistically that's early June.

Aisha

subject: Closing the loop
body:
Hi Jackson,

I've reached out a couple of times without connecting, so I'll assume the timing isn't right. If production scheduling across your Oakland line ever comes up, I've attached a two-page overview of how a small manufacturer cut changeover planning from a day to an hour.

If someone else handles operations tools, a name would be much appreciated. Otherwise I'll close the loop here.

Jenna

subject: Re: Stark three-year expansion: agreement out for signature
body:
Jenna,

Sorry for the silence. The agreement is fine on our side, but multi-year commitments now go through our new capital review board, which meets monthly, and we missed the April slot. I'll push for May, but I can't promise it. There's nothing for you to do right now; I'll come back to you once it's on the agenda.

Priya

subject: Checking in ahead of your Q4 planning
body:
Hi Robert,

I know the budget freeze put everything on hold in March, and I'm not looking to restart anything before you're ready. I wanted to share one thing: we've launched a lighter mid-market package that starts at about 40% of the quote you saw, with the same shipment-tracking workflows your team liked.

I'll reconnect in September, ahead of your Q4 planning.

All the best,
Mike

subject: Extra logins for the summer season
body:
Hi Tom,

Hope the spring rush has been kind to you. With summer bookings coming up, a few agencies your size add two or three seasonal logins for June through August and remove them in September. If that's useful, I can set it up so the extra seats only run for those months.

No need if your current twelve cover it.

Jenna

subject: Re: Extra logins for the summer season
body:
Hi Jenna,

Good thought, thanks. Twelve should cover us this year, since we've moved two part-timers onto the reservations desk full time and they already have logins. If the new Breckenridge office opens before August I'll shout, because they would need two more.

Tom

subject: Wayne Enterprises MSA: responses to your redlines
body:
Hi Elaine,

Thank you for the detailed markup. Attached are our responses. In short: we accept your governing-law change to Delaware, we've moved the liability cap to the greater of twelve months of fees or $1M, and we've added regional data residency language for the EMEA and APAC units.

We can't accept unlimited liability for data breaches, but we've offered a separate super-cap at three times annual fees. Happy to walk your team through the reasoning.

Best,
Mike Davis

subject: Getting more out of your Black Mesa trial
body:
Hi Noah,

I noticed your trial workspace has a couple of projects set up but not much activity this week. Many research labs start with our lab-inventory template, which sets up sample tracking and equipment booking in about ten minutes. Here's the link, plus a three-minute video.

If someone else on your team is the right person to evaluate this, I'm happy to talk with them too.

Mike

subject: Vendor review pack for Sterling Cooper
body:
Hi Joan,

Mason suggested I send our vendor review pack directly to you. It includes our completed standard security questionnaire, insurance certificates, the MSA with Mason's requested changes marked up, and a summary of our SOC 2 Type II report.

If your team uses its own questionnaire, send it over and we'll turn it around within five business days. I'm also happy to set up a call with our legal counsel if that's faster for the MSA.

Best regards,
Sophie

subject: Approval workflows for the holiday range
body:
Hi Charlotte,

Layla mentioned you're planning the holiday range and might want approval workflows across the e-commerce and brand teams. I've attached a short example of how another confectionery brand runs its seasonal sign-offs on the team plan, from first draft to retailer-ready assets.

If it looks relevant, I can switch your workspace to a 30-day team trial so you can try it on real work rather than a demo.

Best,
Sophie

subject: Webinar recording and campaign planning template
body:
Hi Natalie,

Thanks for joining our campaign operations webinar. Here's the recording and the planning template we walked through; a lot of agencies adapt it for client retainers.

If your agency is reviewing its project tools this year, I'd love to speak with whoever owns that decision. Would you be open to introducing me to your director of operations?

Thanks,
Jenna

subject: Spacely Tech: our counter-offer
body:
Hi Mia,

Thanks for the candid conversation on Monday. I took your request back to our deal desk. We can't get to 15%, but we can offer 8% off list across the 120 seats, plus extended terms: a 24-month agreement with the second year's price held flat.

I think that's a strong position for both of us. Let me know how Derek feels about it and I can turn the order form around the same day.

Mike

subject: Dunder Mifflin regional licence: agreement attached
body:
Hi Liam,

Great to finally be at this point. Attached is the regional licence agreement for your three branches: 60 seats at 42k a year, with the training sessions for your sales team included. You mentioned you can sign up to 50k yourself, so this should be a straightforward one.

If it's easier, I can send it through DocuSign instead of the PDF. Happy to jump on a call if Siobhán has any questions on the terms.

Cheers,
Mike

subject: Re: Dunder Mifflin regional licence: agreement attached
body:
Mike,

Got it, thanks. I'll have a read over the weekend. DocuSign would be grand, so send it that way when you get a chance. It might be a week or two before I sign, as we're in the middle of the quarter-end push here and Siobhán wants a look at the renewal clause, but no concerns so far.

Liam

subject: Blue Sun: 45 minutes on data residency?
body:
Hi Ingrid,

Hudson introduced us a few weeks ago. I know your team is deep in audit season, so I'll keep this short. Our security lead would like 45 minutes to walk you through regional data residency and key management for the multi-region rollout. I've attached our latest SOC 2 report and a completed CAIQ so you can review ahead of time.

Any slot in May works on our side.

Best,
Mike Davis

subject: Re: Vendor review pack for Sterling Cooper
body:
Sophie,

Received, thank you. Our legal team has comments on the indemnity and limitation of liability clauses and will come back with redlines once they've cleared their current backlog. I don't have a timeline yet. Please route anything further through me rather than Mason, so we keep a single thread on our side.

Joan Harlan
Head of Procurement

subject: Proposal: follow-up questions
body:
Sophie,

Our team has reviewed your proposal. Follow-up questions are attached, mostly about payment terms, the cap on renewal increases and the reference customers you mentioned. Answers within the next few weeks would suit our planning.

Caleb Wright

subject: Re: Proposal: follow-up questions
body:
Hi Caleb,

Thank you for your patience. Our answers to the follow-up questions are attached. In summary: we invoice annually in advance on 30-day terms, renewal increases are capped at 5%, and two reference customers in Japan have agreed to take a call.

Happy to set up the reference calls whenever suits you.

Best,
Sophie

subject: Trial results for Javier
body:
Hi Sofia,

Congratulations on getting the summer campaign out through the trial workspace. Lucía's numbers are impressive: three campaign launches in four weeks, with approval time down from six days to two.

I've put those results into a two-page summary you could share with Javier. Would it help if I joined the conversation with him, or would you rather present it yourself?

Jenna

subject: Following up on your meeting with our CRO
body:
Dear Isabella,

Thank you for hosting our CRO in Milan. He came away convinced that the strategic initiative is the right next step for both of us. As agreed, Giulia will receive our comments on the framework agreement this week, and Francesca and I will start the programme plan for phase one.

Is September still the target for your board?

Cordiali saluti,
Sophie Turner

subject: Re: Pilot terms for the EMEA pilot
body:
Dear Ms Turner,

Anna Müller forwarded the pilot terms you sent in April, and I have read them for her. Two questions on the commercial side: please confirm that the pilot fee is credited against a subscription if we continue, and send the pilot order form with the eight-week term.

Best regards,
Jonas Becker

subject: Risk assessment pack for the LATAM pilot
body:
Olá Fernanda,

Lucas suggested I send our risk assessment pack directly to you. It includes our responses aligned to the central bank's cloud outsourcing rules, the business continuity plan summary, and our data residency options for Brazil.

If your team needs anything in Portuguese, we can arrange it. Would a call with our risk lead be useful?

Atenciosamente,
Sophie Turner

subject: Introducing Owen Burnett
body:
Hi Mike,

Following up on our May call. I know I was vague about the initiative. It's now been scoped: we're overhauling our deal-desk process across the investment banking group. Owen Burnett, our chief of staff, owns it, so I'm handing the conversation over to him. He's copied here and expects to hear from you.

Ryan

subject: Mom Corp MSA: final redlines
body:
Hi Walter,

Attached are our final comments on the MSA. We've accepted your changes to the confidentiality and governing-law clauses, and we've met you halfway on the liability cap at eighteen months of fees. The only change we can't take is unilateral price changes at renewal, but we've offered a 5% cap on any increase instead.

Audrey has the order form, so we're close.

Best,
Mike

subject: Questions on API rate limits
body:
Hi Sophie,

I'm the data engineer who'd be building our pipelines if Hyperion goes ahead. I read the technical FAQ Benjamin shared. Two questions: are rate limits per user or per organisation, and can we request higher limits for nightly batch loads of flight data? We'd be pulling roughly 2 million records a night.

Nadia Petrov

subject: Equipment scheduling for Cyberdyne's R&D labs
body:
Hi Neil,

Thanks for raising your hand on our June outreach. You mentioned your R&D labs juggle shared test rigs across three teams with a spreadsheet. That's exactly where our scheduling module earns its keep: bookings, maintenance windows and usage reporting in one place.

Would 30 minutes next week work for a discovery call? I'd like to understand how many engineers book rigs and who owns the budget for lab tooling.

Mike Davis

subject: 50 additional seats: co-terming with your November renewal
body:
Hi Rachael,

Following your conversation with Hannah, here's how we'd add the 50 research seats. Rather than a separate agreement, we'd co-term them with your November renewal, so the new seats start in July at a prorated price and everything renews on one date.

I've copied Owen, since procurement will want to review the structure. Happy to walk through the numbers whenever suits.

Jenna

subject: Pilot locations and rollout order
body:
Hi Dale,

Stella asked me to work with you on the multi-site pilot. To plan the rollout, could you send the eight locations you'd like in the pilot and their opening hours? We usually start with two stores in week one, then add three each week, so Mona can release budget in stages.

Once I have the list, I'll draft a four-week schedule.

Jenna

subject: Deep-dive demo agenda: API and event streams
body:
Hi Thomas,

As promised, here's the agenda for the deep-dive demo. We'll spend most of the time in the API: authentication, rate limits, webhooks and the event stream, with a live example syncing records into a sample service. Our solutions architect will run it, so feel free to go off script.

Would Thursday at 1pm work, and should Hannah and Victor join?

Sophie

subject: Rekall sales ops suite: final proposal
body:
Hi Douglas,

Following last week's demo, here's our final proposal for the sales ops suite: 40 seats on annual billing and a dedicated onboarding manager for the first 60 days. Ethan's team has reviewed the scope.

I'd love to get this signed before your Q3 kickoff so the reps start the quarter on the new suite. Any questions, just let me know.

Sophie

subject: Evaluation plan for your propulsion test teams
body:
Hi Raymond,

Thanks for the discovery call. As agreed, here's a three-week evaluation plan: week one sets up your test-scheduling workflow with Tyler, week two runs it on two live test campaigns, and week three reviews the results with your leads.

Before we talk commercials, could you confirm who holds budget authority for this? Until then there's nothing for Sandra to review.

Jenna

subject: Validated systems pack for Umbrella
body:
Dear Helen,

James mentioned that your quality and compliance team signs off any new vendor before procurement proceeds. Attached is our validated systems pack: the GxP assessment, our computer system validation summary, the 21 CFR Part 11 controls mapping and the audit trail specification.

If your team uses its own vendor assessment template, I'll gladly complete it. Would a call with our compliance lead be useful?

Kind regards,
Sophie Turner

subject: Shop-floor demo for your production team
body:
Hi Zoe,

Thanks for the conversation about your production scheduling. Following your pricing request, I'd suggest a shop-floor demo for Fiona's team before we go further: work orders, machine scheduling and shift handovers, using a sample of your own product lines.

Would the week of June 15 work? It would be great to have Graham there for the last half hour.

Best,
Sophie

subject: Re: Trial results for Javier
body:
Hi Jenna,

Thank you, the summary is great. I'll present it to Javier on Friday myself, since he prefers to hear it from the team, but please send him the proposal directly afterwards. He'll want to see the annual pricing for 20 users and whether we can keep the trial workflows without rebuilding them.

Sofia

subject: Deal-desk overhaul: agenda for a working session
body:
Hi Owen,

Ryan tells me you own the deal-desk overhaul. I'd suggest a 60-minute working session rather than a demo: you walk us through how a deal moves from term sheet to approval today, and we show where approvals, conflict checks and audit trails could live in one workflow.

Would the week of June 8 work? If Elena will run it day to day, it would be worth having her there.

Best,
Mike Davis

subject: Phase 2 rollout: planning workshop
body:
Hi Rachel,

Great to meet you on Friday's intro call. As you said, Phase 2 is a separate conversation from the Phase 1 paperwork, and it makes sense to start planning now so nothing waits once you're ready.

I'd suggest a two-hour workshop with you and Samir to map the regional offices, rollout order and seat counts. Could you do the week of June 8?

Best,
Jenna

subject: Sister lab expansion: what the research add-on covers
body:
Hi Dr. Connors,

Olivia suggested I introduce myself ahead of the July QBR. Her team has used the research lab add-on since April for sample tracking and protocol versioning, and she thought your genomics lab might want the same setup.

I'd be glad to show you what her team built in a 30-minute call. No preparation needed on your side.

Best,
Jenna Lopez

subject: POC results write-up
body:
Sophie,

Attached is our engineers' write-up from the POC. In short: it met eleven of the twelve criteria, and the twelfth is a configuration question that Amanda believes is solvable. I'm recommending we proceed to our internal review board. Carl runs that process; expect him to contact you. It's slow, so plan for August.

Daniel

subject: Q3 implementation: presentation date
body:
Hi Ruby,

You mentioned on the webinar that you're aiming for a Q3 implementation. To keep that realistic, I'd suggest we present the full plan to you and your plant manager in mid-June: brewing schedule management, inventory tracking for raw materials, and how the rollout would fit around your summer production peak.

Would June 10 or 11 work?

Sophie

subject: Re: Wayne Enterprises MSA: responses to your redlines
body:
Mike,

Apologies for the long gap; the rollout went through our global IT steering review in May. We accept your position on the liability cap and the super-cap. Two items remain: the DPA must name sub-processors per region, and we need a termination right if a sub-processor changes without 30 days' notice.

If you can agree to both, I can recommend signature to Marcus.

Elaine Vance
Associate General Counsel

subject: Hephaestus: commercial proposal
body:
Hi Rosa,

Thanks for joining the final session of the deep dive. Attached is the commercial proposal: 110 seats across your three engineering groups, the CAD integration pack, and a structured rollout over the summer so your teams aren't disrupted mid-project.

Ian mentioned the board reviews new commitments in July. If that's the target, we'd want terms agreed by early July. Happy to adjust the rollout order if needed.

Mike

subject: Re: Questions on API rate limits
body:
Hi Nadia,

Great questions. Rate limits are per organisation, and on the analytics platform tier we raise them for scheduled batch jobs: 2 million records a night is well within what we can configure. Our bulk API is also a better fit for that volume than the standard endpoints.

I'll ask our solutions architect to send you sample code. Would that help before the presentation on June 24?

Sophie

subject: Workday connector walkthrough
body:
Hi Caroline,

Aisha suggested I reach out now that planning is done. I'd love to show you our Workday connector: how new hires are provisioned, how leavers are removed on their last day, and how field mappings are managed without code.

Would 45 minutes next week work? If Doug looks after SSO, it would help to have him there too.

Best,
Jenna

subject: Re: Deep-dive demo agenda: API and event streams
body:
Sophie,

Thursday at 1pm works. Hannah will join; her team would build on it. Victor will join for the last 20 minutes since he signs off new tools. Please show event replay and how webhooks behave under load, those are the questions I'll be asked.

Thomas

subject: Thank you: committee materials
body:
Dear Watanabe-san,

Thank you for your time yesterday with our solutions engineer. As requested, I've attached two references from regional banks and the full pricing schedule for our proposal. We will answer Sato-san's vendor risk questions as soon as they arrive, so the committee has everything well before July 14.

With best regards,
Sophie Turner

subject: Re: Pilot terms for the EMEA pilot
body:
Dear Mr Becker,

Thank you for the careful review. I can confirm that the pilot fee is credited in full against a subscription if Hooli continues after the eight weeks. The pilot order form with the eight-week term is attached.

If useful, I can join a call to answer anything else.

Kind regards,
Sophie Turner

subject: Re: POC results write-up
body:
Hi Daniel,

Thank you, that's a great result, and thanks to Amanda and the team for the rigour. Our solutions architect will work through the twelfth criterion with Amanda next week, so it's settled before the review board.

I'll prepare whatever Carl needs. August works on our side; we'll hold the pricing in the proposal until then.

Best,
Sophie

subject: Re: Evaluation plan for your propulsion test teams
body:
Jenna,

The plan works. Tyler can start on June 16. On budget: I'm still confirming who signs off, so let's hold any paperwork until I know. One requirement up front: we need ITAR-compliant data hosting for anything touching test data.

Raymond Cho

subject: Re: Equipment scheduling for Cyberdyne's R&D labs
body:
Mike,

Next Tuesday at 10 works. Around 45 engineers book rigs today, and lab tooling sits in my operating budget, though anything over 50k needs our VP's sign-off. Rebecca in IT forwarded your earlier newsletters to me, so I've seen the scheduling overview already. Please bring pricing tiers if you can.

Neil

subject: Startup bundle: proposal for 15 seats
body:
Hi Jared,

Carlos mentioned you hold the budget for new tools, so I wanted to send this directly. Attached is our startup bundle proposal: 15 seats at 12k for the first year, which includes our Series A discount of 30% off list. It also locks that rate for a second year if you grow past 25 seats.

Happy to walk you through it in 20 minutes whenever suits.

Jenna

subject: EMEA rollout: seat plan by country
body:
Hi Hannah,

Sarah suggested I work with you on the seat plan for the EMEA expansion. To size it properly, could you share headcount for the Amsterdam, Munich and Lyon sites and which teams go live first? We'd also want to know whether Sarah signs for all three sites or each site has its own budget.

Once we have that, I'll turn it into a phased proposal for Sarah to review.

Mike

subject: Re: Q3 implementation: presentation date
body:
Hi Sophie,

June 10 works. Leonard Kowalski, our plant manager, will join, and he'll have lots of questions about the brewing floor. Carla in finance will need numbers before anything is approved, so bring an outline of pricing too. Thanks for keeping it practical.

Ruby

subject: Re: 50 additional seats: co-terming with your November renewal
body:
Jenna,

Co-terming is our preference, thanks. Two requests: show the prorated amount for July to November as a separate line, and confirm the per-seat rate for the new seats matches the existing contract. If so, Rachael can approve the expansion and we'll fold it into the November renewal.

Owen Price
Senior Procurement Manager

subject: Re: Pilot locations and rollout order
body:
Jenna,

Attached is the list. Start with Gresham and Beaverton; their managers are keen and free in July. Avoid the downtown location until week three, as they're short-staffed through June. Mona in finance will want to see pricing for all eight before Stella signs off.

Dale

subject: Framework agreement: our comments
body:
Dear Giulia,

As Isabella agreed with our CRO, attached are our comments on the framework agreement. We've accepted Italian governing law and the confidentiality terms. Our main comments concern the scope of the liability cap and the right to audit, where we've proposed a yearly remote audit instead of on-site visits.

I'm happy to arrange a call with our counsel.

Kind regards,
Sophie

subject: Re: Shop-floor demo for your production team
body:
Hi Sophie,

Zoe forwarded your note. I run production systems here, so the demo would be with me and two shift leads. Tuesday 16 June in the morning works. Graham is away that week, so he'll want a written proposal afterwards instead.

Cheers,
Fiona Clarke

subject: Re: Wayne Enterprises MSA: responses to your redlines
body:
Hi Elaine,

Good news on both points. Our counsel has agreed to list sub-processors per region in Schedule 3 of the DPA, and to the termination right on 30 days' notice of a sub-processor change. Updated drafts are attached with those two changes tracked and nothing else touched.

If these work, I'll prepare execution copies for Marcus.

Mike

subject: Re: Workday connector walkthrough
body:
Jenna,

Wednesday the 10th at 2pm works for me, and I've asked Doug to join. Please come prepared to show custom field mappings: we track lab certifications in Workday and would want them to carry over. That's the deciding factor for us.

Caroline

subject: Re: Rekall sales ops suite: final proposal
body:
Sophie,

We're aligned on scope and price. Ethan is handling our internal approvals; I expect signature by the end of June, maybe a week later given the holiday. Please have the 40 user accounts on Melina's list ready by kickoff, as the reps will log in from day one.

Douglas Quinn
VP Sales

subject: Re: Phase 2 rollout: planning workshop
body:
Jenna,

The week of June 8 is tight; Samir could do Thursday the 11th for an hour, and I'd join the second half. Start with the London and Singapore offices, which have the most users and the least patience. Please don't treat this as a commitment; the Phase 2 budget isn't approved until Q4.

Rachel

subject: Oceanic: recordkeeping requirements mapped to the logistics suite
body:
Hi Kate,

Thanks for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is the written mapping of your recordkeeping requirements to the logistics suite, line by line. Immutable audit history on cargo manifests and seven-year retention are both covered by the enterprise tier; the two items marked amber need a configuration change rather than new development.

Once you've reviewed it, should we bring Owen and your procurement team in?

Mike

subject: Re: Validated systems pack for Umbrella
body:
Sophie,

Thank you, this is unusually thorough for a first submission. We'll need our standard supplier quality questionnaire completed as well, which James will send. A call with your compliance lead would help; Thursday afternoon suits. After that I expect to recommend approval.

Helen Ashworth

subject: Re: Sister lab expansion: what the research add-on covers
body:
Jenna,
